items.quote: The Māori-language name for Auckland is Tāmaki Makaurau
items.note: "Tāmaki" alone is also widely used as a short form; decide in advance whether to accept it.

items.quote: Auckland is popularly nicknamed the "City of Sails" or the "Queen City"
items.note: "Queen City" is also a nickname, but the yachting clue rules it out.

items.quote: The central part of the urban area occupies a narrow isthmus between the Manukau Harbour on the Tasman Sea and the Waitematā Harbour on the Pacific Ocean
Rangitoto Island is a volcanic island in the Hauraki Gulf near Auckland, New Zealand
items.note: Wikipedia describes it as "a symmetrical shield volcano cone"; "guards the entrance" is colour, not a checkable claim, but nothing else fits.

items.quote: The Sky Tower is a telecommunications and observation tower in Auckland, New Zealand
As the sections were manufactured by a Japanese company, this led to the nickname 'Nippon clip-ons'
The match took place on 23 October 2011 at Eden Park, in Auckland, New Zealand
items.note: 1987 is in en:Eden_Park: "it became the first stadium in the world to host two Rugby World Cup finals, having held the inaugural final in 1987". Eden Park also hosted the 1988 rugby league World Cup final and the 2021 Women's RWC final, but only it fits both 1987 and 2011.

items.quote: In 1865, Auckland was replaced by Wellington as the capital
"Royals" is the debut single by New Zealand singer-songwriter Lorde
items.note: Her North Shore upbringing (Devonport and Bayswater) is in en:Lorde.

items.quote: Maungawhau / Mount Eden is a scoria cone
items.note: Since the 2014 Treaty settlement the official name is the dual "Maungawhau / Mount Eden", so "better known by" is fair but no longer the official name alone.
